chains.title: GABPA/ETS alt-gain activates TERT

links.claim: GABPA binds the alt A allele more strongly. GABPA has its own QBiC-SELEX model at this base with an alt-gain (effect +4.01, z 68.47; E33), and published work identifies a de novo ETS motif and the GABP tetramer as the activator at mutant TERT promoters (E34a, E34b, E34e). Caveat: no ENCODE ChIP-seq peak over this exact base is from a glioblastoma or otherwise matching biosample (E04); GABPA peaks over the variant are only from other biosamples (E11).

The variant lies in promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 with active chromatin marks (DNase, H3K27ac, H3K4me3) and dense TF occupancy; Ensembl independently annotates a TERT promoter regulatory feature. Caveat: E03 z-scores are maxima over ENCODE biosamples, not glioblastoma-specific.
The cCRE is 0 kb from the TERT TSS and the variant is annotated as a TERT upstream_gene_variant in the TERT promoter, making TERT the direct target gene.

GABPA is expressed in DepMap glioblastoma lines (15.52 TPM, rank 303/1626; E17), and GABP-dependent TERT promoter activation has been reported across TERTp-mutant cancer cell lines (E34b), although the provided ChIP data do not include a matched glioblastoma biosample (E04).

Alt-enhanced GABP/ETS binding at the TERT promoter increases TERT transcription and telomerase activity: GABP tetramer is reported to be responsible for promoter activation at recurrent TERTp mutations, and its assembly at the promoter is associated with TERT reactivation and hTERT hyperactivation.

chains.title: ETV3/ETS alt-gain activates TERT

links.claim: ETV3's best QBiC-SELEX model predicts that the alt A allele binds more strongly (effect +2.121, z 166.19; E28), but that model is a CIS-BP-mapped ETV5 model shared identically with other ETS paralogs, so this is family-level ETS evidence rather than ETV3-specific evidence. ETV3 occupancy at this base is unknown because ENCODE never assayed ETV3; no ChIP peak is available.

The variant lies in promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 with active chromatin marks and dense TF occupancy, consistent with a functional TERT promoter element; E03 z-scores are maxima over biosamples, not glioblastoma-specific.
The element is 0 kb from the TERT TSS and the variant is annotated as a TERT upstream_gene_variant in the TERT promoter, making TERT the direct target.
ETV3 is expressed at a modest level in DepMap glioblastoma lines (8.69 TPM, rank 521/1626; E28), so the cell type is permissive, but no ETV3-specific disease or occupancy data are provided.
If ETV3 rather than GABPA occupied the alt-gained ETS site, it could increase TERT expression, but no ETV3-specific occupancy, perturbation, or TERT-output evidence supports this chain.

grades_v0.reason: QBiC-SELEX gives a large alt-gain for the best model (z 166.19, effect +2.121, E17), direction consistent with the claim, but there is no occupancy over this variant in any glioblastoma/matching biosample: E04 states no ENCODE biosample matches the expression context and no peak counts as bound here, and E11's GABPA peaks are only in HepG2/SK-N-SH. SELEX alone is at best weak. Worse, the winning model is a CIS-BP-mapped ETV5 model shared identically (z 166.19, effect 2.121) by ETV2, ETV3 and FLI1 (E27-E29), so it is a family-level ETS prediction, not GABPA-specific evidence.

E03 places the variant inside PLS cCRE EH38E3622530 with DNase z 4.8, H3K27ac z 4.2, H3K4me3 z 4.5, and E04 confirms 121 TF peaks over the base; E01 independently annotates a TERT promoter regulatory feature. Caveat: the z-scores are maxima over biosamples, not glioblastoma-specific.
E02 puts the variant 0.0 kb from the TERT TSS and E01 assigns an upstream TERT transcript consequence inside the TERT promoter cCRE; TERT is the immediately adjacent gene.

GABPA expression in DepMap glioblastoma is documented (15.52 TPM, rank 303/1626, E17), which supports the cell-type premise, but the second half of the claim (recurrence of TERT promoter mutations in glioblastoma/melanoma/bladder) rests on E15, which is only a Europe PMC hit list of titles, not a result establishing recurrence.

The claim that alt-enhanced ETS/GABPA binding raises TERT transcription and telomerase activity is supported only by E15, a list of unrelated review/title hits with no allele-specific or perturbation measurement. Nothing cited connects GABPA occupancy at this base to TERT output or to disease.

Only a QBiC-SELEX prediction (E28, z 166.19, effect +2.121, alt-gain) with occupancy explicitly unknown (ENCODE never assayed ETV3). The model used is a CIS-BP-mapped ETV5 model shared identically with GABPA/ETV2/FLI1, so the prediction does not distinguish ETV3 from other ETS factors; no occupancy evidence exists at all.
Same as H1: E03 shows the variant in PLS cCRE EH38E3622530 with active marks, E04 shows dense TF occupancy, E01 annotates the TERT promoter.
E02 (TERT at 0.0 kb) plus E01 (upstream TERT consequence in the promoter cCRE) make TERT the direct target.
ETV3 expression in glioblastoma lines is shown (8.69 TPM, rank 521, E28), but the disease-relevance half again rests on the E15 title list only.
No cited evidence links ETV3 binding at this base to TERT expression or to telomerase activation; E15 provides no ETV3 or allele-specific functional data.

Only a QBiC-SELEX prediction (E30, z -36.84, effect -1.289, ref binds more) with occupancy unknown (never assayed); the model is a CIS-BP-mapped TFAP2E model, not TFAP2A's own. Direction (ref-gain) is consistent with the loss-of-site claim, but there is no occupancy data of any kind, and the 'repressor' premise for TFAP2A at TERT is not evidenced.
E03/E04/E01 place the variant in an active promoter-like cCRE at the TERT promoter.
E02 and E01 assign the element immediately upstream of TERT (0.0 kb).
TFAP2A is expressed in glioblastoma lines (9.65 TPM, rank 479, E30); the recurrence claim again relies only on the E15 title list.
The derepression model (loss of TFAP2A site -> more TERT -> telomerase) has no cited support: E15 contains no TFAP2A functional data, and no evidence is given that TFAP2A represses TERT at all.

QBiC-SELEX shows ref-gain (E19, z -14.7, effect -1.719), consistent with the direction claimed, but occupancy is only in DOHH2 (E13), not a glioblastoma biosample, and the local cCRE CTCF signal is low (z 2.0 in a PLS, E03). SELEX plus a non-matching-biosample peak is weak, not supported.
E03/E04/E01 place the variant in active PLS EH38E3622530 at the TERT promoter; note the element is classified promoter-like, not a CTCF/insulator element, which undercuts the insulation framing.
E02 (0.0 kb from TERT TSS) and E01 (TERT upstream consequence) support TERT as target.
CTCF expression in glioblastoma lines is shown (26.45 TPM, E19/E13), but disease relevance again rests on the E15 title list only, and no CTCF occupancy is shown in this cell type.

The claim that reduced CTCF binding weakens insulation/repression and raises TERT is entirely unevidenced; E15 provides no CTCF or insulator data, and the variant is in a promoter cCRE with weak CTCF signal.

grades_final.reason: GABPA has its own QBiC-SELEX model at this base with a clear alt-gain (effect +4.01, z 68.47, rank 5/997; E33), and the literature quotes directly state that TERTp mutations create a de novo ETS motif and that the GABP tetramer is the factor responsible for activation at mutant TERT promoters across 53 cell lines/16 cancer types (E34a, E34b, E34e). ENCODE ChIP peaks over the variant exist (HepG2, SK-N-SH; E11) though not in a glioblastoma biosample (E04); the family-level GABP occupancy literature plus the TF's own SELEX model in the correct direction is the strongest available support, so this is not a prediction-only link. The stated caveat (no matched-biosample ChIP) is correctly acknowledged and does not overturn the claim.

E03 places the variant inside PLS cCRE EH38E3622530 with high DNase/H3K27ac/H3K4me3 z-scores, and E01 independently annotates a TERT promoter regulatory feature overlapping the site; E04 shows dense TF occupancy in a PLS class element. The caveat that z-scores are biosample maxima is a limitation on cell-type specificity, not on the element annotation claim as stated.
E02 gives TERT at 0.0 kb from its TSS and E01 annotates the variant as a TERT upstream_gene_variant in the TERT promoter; the element-to-gene assignment is direct and needs no intervening gene.

GABPA expression in glioblastoma lines is shown (15.52 TPM, rank 303/1626; E17) and GABP-dependent TERTp activation is reported across many TERTp-mutant cancer cell lines (E34b), but the quotes do not establish that glioblastoma lines were among those tested, and the ChIP evidence over this base comes only from HepG2/SK-N-SH (E04, E11). Cell-type relevance is therefore plausible but indirect rather than directly demonstrated for glioblastoma.

Functional literature is quoted: the GABP tetramer is responsible for promoter activation at recurrent TERTp mutations (E34b), its assembly at the promoter is associated with TERT reactivation (E34e), and TERTp mutations hyperactivate hTERT (E34c). Direction is consistent (alt-gained ETS site -> more GABP -> more TERT). This is literature-level functional evidence rather than a variant-specific perturbation, but it is the appropriate evidence class here and it directly speaks to the claimed effect.

The only support is a QBiC-SELEX alt-gain (effect +2.121, z 166.19) obtained from a CIS-BP-mapped ETV5 model that is shared identically with other ETS paralogs (E27-E29 vs E28); ETV3 has unknown occupancy (ENCODE never assayed it) and no ChIP peak over the variant. This is an in vitro prediction plus family-level ETS motif logic, and the chain offers no reason to prefer ETV3 over the paralogs or over GABPA whose own model exists.

E03/E04 place the variant in PLS cCRE EH38E3622530 with active chromatin marks and dense occupancy, and E01 annotates a TERT promoter feature; the element call is independent of which TF binds and is directly supported (biosample-max caveat noted but does not affect this link).
E02 puts TERT at 0.0 kb from the TSS and E01 annotates the variant as a TERT upstream_gene_variant, making TERT the direct target of this element.

ETV3 is expressed in DepMap glioblastoma lines (8.69 TPM, rank 521/1626; E28), which shows the cell type is permissive, but no ETV3 occupancy, perturbation or disease data in glioblastoma (or any TERTp-relevant cancer) are provided, so the link rests on expression context alone.

No evidence is cited (evidence_ids empty) and none of the supplied records shows ETV3 occupancy, ETV3 perturbation, or ETV3-dependent TERT output; the claim is explicitly conditional and speculative, so nothing bears on it.
